attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own newsletter, giving his updated hypothesis. The NYT quote that follows is separate and is not the claim.

semantics.note: Keeps 'have to raise', the antecedent, the size threshold and the July 2025 horizon. 'I believe ... will' states an unqualified expectation of a definite outcome, not graded confidence, so it is a scored forecast.

contract.note: The thresholds ($6.6B, 2025-07-31) come from the speaker and OpenAI's announcement. The 'need' half can only be tested against OpenAI's own stated need, and the contract says so openly. The raise half is clear on any reading: $40B, with a $10B first closing.

evidence.note: Company disclosure dated 2024-10-02 that the $6.6B round was raised. This meets the antecedent and sets the threshold. It is evidence of the condition, not of the outcome.
OpenAI's own statement on 2024-12-27, inside the horizon, that it needed to raise more capital. It is a company disclosure, gives no amount and is not an independent finding of necessity.
OpenAI announced $40B of new funding on 2025-03-31, inside the horizon and well above $6.6B. Company disclosure.

Lead investor disclosed a definitive agreement signed 2025-03-31 for up to $40B, with a $10B first closing planned for mid-April 2025. This meets the contract's test for a raised round. The packet does not confirm the closing was paid.

output.rationale: The antecedent was met when the $6.6B round was announced on 2024-10-02. Inside the horizon, OpenAI said it needed more capital (Dec 2024) and announced a $40B round (Mar 2025). SoftBank disclosed a signed agreement with a $10B first closing planned for April 2025. That meets the support condition. Necessity rests only on OpenAI's own disclosure, and the packet does not confirm the closing was paid, but under the frozen contract the forecast holds.
